Change c0114. Location: 1818 Vol. I, Ch. V; 1831 Ch. VI.

Context before (unchanged): This girl had always been the favourite of her father; but, through a strange perversity, her mother could not endure her, and, after the death of M. Moritz, treated her very ill.

1818 text: My aunt observed this; and, when Justine was twelve years of age, prevailed on her mother to allow her to live at her house.

1831 text: My aunt observed this; and, when Justine was twelve years of age, prevailed on her mother to allow her to live at our house.

Diff: My aunt observed this; and, when Justine was twelve years of age, prevailed on her mother to allow her to live at [-her-] {+our+} house.

Context after (unchanged): The republican institutions of our country have produced simpler and happier manners than those which prevail in the great monarchies that surround it.

result.rationale: Replacing 'her house' with 'our house' changes the referent: Justine now lives in the narrator's family home rather than the aunt's, slightly shifting her status as a household member. Mostly a pronoun swap with minor characterization effect.
